newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to lift farm product export ban by July 1.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to lift farm product export ban by July 1.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to lift all export bans on farm products by July 1 in line with a $659 million funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund, a government spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"Under a decree approved by the interim cabinet today Bulgaria is committed to lifting gradually all export bans on agricultural products by July 1," the spokeswoman told reporters.
Export bans on agricultural products as a way of controlling shortages and external deficits would be replaced gradually by a licensing regime and an introduction of export fees.
Under the accord signed on March 17 Bulgaria is expected to liberalise trade and pricing policy to be carried out by the new government after April 19 elections.

In a move to offset grain and other shortages the government pledged to abolish price controls on farm produce for the coming harvest season and let prices be determined by the market, reflecting international prices.

The IMF package envisages a $148 million Compensatory and Contingency Financing Facility to enable Bulgaria to pay for grain imports. Uncontrolled grain exports two years ago and a bad harvest last year produced an acute grain shortage this year which the interim cabinet has so far controlled.
